# UK Public Backs AI to Transform Government Services, But Fears Losing the Human Touch


New Pega research finds citizens see opportunities for faster, more efficient services but want transparency, accountability, and human involvement in important AI-driven decisions


**LONDON, UK. – November 24, 2026** **–** UK citizens are encouraged about how AI could transform public services but want safeguards and responsible use of the technology, according to new research from[Pegasystems Inc.](https://www.pega.com/) (NASDAQ: PEGA), the enterprise AI software company for mission-critical work.


The study, conducted by HarrisX among more than 2,000 UK citizens aged 18 or over, found optimism around AI’s potential. More than half (53%) said AI could help deliver public services more quickly, while 51% also believe it could help reduce running costs. This suggests the UK government should think beyond incremental productivity improvements and consider how AI can fundamentally enable the redesign of public service delivery.


Other findings further signal that UK citizens want to see transformative change with AI that doesn’t simply automate existing processes but breaks down bureaucratic bottlenecks and roadblocks. Notably, more than 1 in 2 (57%) are comfortable with government using existing information to pre-fill forms and 48% support relevant information sharing between public bodies.


People with positive AI experiences in their personal lives are fueling the appetite for it in public services. Among regular AI users, nearly two thirds (61%) believe AI could improve overall quality of public services, compared with just 17% of those who never use AI. Regular AI users are more likely to believe AI could make services faster (70%) and reduce running costs (64%). However, only 18% of regular AI users want AI introduced into public services as quickly as possible, compared with 10% of all respondents.


Other findings highlighted what citizens expect from the use of AI in public services, including:


-


**Citizens want human-centred service delivery:** 79% believe greater use of AI could mean fewer opportunities to speak to someone directly. At the same time, 47% believe human staff members should make final decisions on matters that could have a major impact on someone’s life, such as grants, mental-health support, and benefits.


-


**Transparency can help build confidence in how AI is used by government:** Almost half of respondents (48%) said clear information about when and how AI is being used in public services would increase their confidence.


-


**Younger citizens more convinced AI will reshape public services positively:** Gen Z respondents are more optimistic than Baby Boomers, with 55% of 18–24-year-olds believing AI could help deliver public services more quickly, compared with 43% of those aged 55 and over. This reflects a wider generational divide in AI use, with 62% of Gen Z using AI every day or a few times a week, compared with 29% of Baby Boomers.


To help public-sector organisations respond to these expectations, Pega’s government solutions are specifically designed to future-proof public services. Opening new avenues for organisational value through transformative solutions, including Generative AI, public sector organizations can effectively tackle backlogs, drive substantial productivity gains, and enhance service quality. By mapping processes, data requirements, and user roles before development begins, the toolkit helps organisations modernise services, improve efficiency, and maintain greater visibility and accountability over how AI is used.


**Quotes & Commentary**


“The public can see the potential for AI to make government services faster, simpler, and more efficient,” said Alex Case, ex-senior civil servant at Number 10 and now senior director, government strategy & industry lead, Pegasystems. “But the real opportunity is much bigger than automating existing tasks or adding AI to outdated processes. It is to fundamentally rethink how government delivers services, using AI to connect systems, streamline decisions, and remove unnecessary bureaucracy.


Case added: “The message from this research is clear: citizens want the benefits of AI, but they also want to know how decisions are made, who is accountable, and when they can speak to a person. Government needs to be more ambitious about transformation while building those safeguards into services from the outset.”


**Notes**


The research was conducted by HarrisX based on the views of 2,008 UK adults in the UK. It explored public attitudes towards the potential benefits and risks of using AI in public services, as well as levels of trust in organisations responsible for overseeing its use.
